case_name: Ignacio Montes G and Alberto Yanez A v. Commissioner
suitability_reason: Only decided issue (C.M.'s residence with petitioners for more than half of 2020) turned entirely on the credibility of petitioners' testimony and lack of documentation; all other 152(c) elements conceded.

taxpayer.filing_status_claimed: head of household (each petitioner's separate return); later-prepared joint return dated May 5, 2022
taxpayer.notes: Notice of deficiency adjusted Montes G's amended return, adding Yanez A's income; notice states examined filing status is joint.

adjustments: added Yanez A's income to Montes G's amended return
disallowed recovery rebate credit (qualifying children and dependents disallowed)
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Whether C.M. was petitioners' qualifying child for 2020 (residency test)
conceded: Respondent: section 6662(a) penalty does not apply (stipulated)
Y.R. was a qualifying relative but not a qualifying child (stipulated)
E.P. not a qualifying child or qualifying relative (stipulated)
Petitioners: A.A.R. not a qualifying child or qualifying relative
Respondent: C.M. satisfies all qualifying child requirements other than same principal place of abode for more than one-half of 2020

findings_of_fact.fact: Montes G's original 2020 return claimed head of household and listed C.C. (C.M.) as nephew for child tax credit
findings_of_fact.snippet: it lists C.C. (subsequently referred to as C.M.) as a nephew qualifying for a child tax credit
On November 18, 2022, respondent issued a Notice of Deficiency to petitioners

findings_of_fact.fact: Respondent conceded every qualifying-child requirement for C.M. except the more-than-half-year shared abode test
findings_of_fact.snippet: C.M. satisfied all the requirements to be a qualifying child other than the requirement that he have the same principal place of abode

findings_of_fact.fact: Montes G testified C.M. lived with petitioners from February 2020 through December 24, 2020; testimony found not credible
findings_of_fact.snippet: He further testified that C.M. lived with petitioners from February 2020 through December 24

findings_of_fact.fact: Court found testimony about C.M.'s residence not credible; no documentation
findings_of_fact.snippet: this Court finds petitioners’ testimony regarding C.M.’s residence with them not credible

issues.question: Was C.M. petitioners' qualifying child under section 152(c) for 2020 (residency test), so as to support child tax credit, EIC and section 6428 recovery rebate credit (other: recovery rebate credit §6428)?
issues.holding: Not a qualifying child: petitioners did not prove C.M. shared their abode for more than half of 2020; no CTC, EIC or recovery rebate credit with respect to C.M.; credits computed only with Y.R. as qualifying relative

amount_determined.description: credits limited to those determined taking into account Y.R.'s status as qualifying relative

issues.computable_reason: Residency finding rests on credibility of testimony and absence of documentation.

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: C.M. not a qualifying child; credits allowed only as computed with Y.R. as qualifying relative; no 6662(a) penalty (conceded).

notes: Facts from First Stipulation of Facts, Stipulation of Settled Issues and trial testimony. Petitioners bore burden; 7491(a) not satisfied. Recovery rebate credit: $1,200 ($2,400 joint) plus $500 per qualifying child under §24(c). Footnote 3: notice inconsistent on filing status (EIC disallowed citing MFS while exam status joint).
